what: Limits for the X3D Phong lighting ladder (tools/lighting_judge.py), committed before any measured run. Every probe scene is a lit 4 x 4 quad seen square-on from a Viewpoint; each witness's picture (8-bit display values, 64 x 64) is compared with the spec oracle's (tools/lighting_oracle.py, X3D 4.0 17.2.2.5) pixel by pixel. Pixels within one pixel of a jump in the oracle's picture (a radius edge, a spot cut-off) are left out of every comparison. Errors are in 8-bit display levels.

readings.linear: colours (Material, light color) are sRGB-coded: decoded, lit, the sum encoded for the display (X3DOM 1.8.3's default, gammaCorrectionDefault 'linear')
readings.display: the lighting equations run on the file's numbers as they are and the sum is shown as it is (the classic OpenGL way)
readings.linear-values: the file's numbers are linear values: lit as they are, the sum encoded for the display (X3DOM 1.8.3 as it ships, X_ITE 16.8.1 with ColorSpace LINEAR). Added 27 Nov 2026 after the first browser recording and before any Blender run.

curves.srgb: the sRGB piecewise curve (IEC 61966-2-1), what Blender's Standard view transform uses
curves.pow22: x^2.2 and x^(1/2.2), what X_ITE 16.8.1 (GAMMA = 2.2) and X3DOM 1.8.3 ('linear') use

blender_exact.why: the add-on's opt-in X3D lighting (EEVEE Material Lighting nodes) must draw the oracle's picture; 8-bit rounding is 0.5 at most

blender_display.why: the same with the display reading (Raw view transform)

browser_agrees.why: a browser is a witness for a reading when it lands this close to the oracle's picture in that reading; which reading each lands on is a finding, not a gate

wrong_twin_default_import.why: the add-on's default import (Principled BSDF, BLENDER light units) must MISS the oracle by this much on falloff and cone scenes, or the probes are too weak to catch an error

expected_fail_cycles_plain.why: with the X3D lighting on, Cycles renders the plain Principled fallback; held to blender_exact's limit it is expected to fail (Jason, 27 Nov 2026: plain for now)

blender_linear_values.why: the add-on's default X3D lighting reading (linear values) must draw the oracle's picture. Added with the reading, before any Blender run.

physical.what: PhysicalMaterial (X3D 4.0 17.2.2.6): X3D's o_i x color x attenuation_i x spot_i around glTF 2.0's metallic-roughness BRDF (Appendix B). Committed 28 Nov 2026 before any PhysicalMaterial run.

spec_reading.why: candela and lux imply 1/d^2 for point and spot lights; radius is X3D's on_i (no range window); spot_i is Table 17.4 for every lighting model; glTF Appendix B writes V as separable Smith-GGX

blender_physical.why: the X3D lighting option's PhysicalMaterial path must draw the spec reading (Blender follows the spec where the spec is clear)

browser_physical.why: a browser witnesses a knob setting when it lands this close; which setting is a finding

wrong_twin_physical_default.why: the default import (Principled BSDF) must miss the spec picture somewhere by 8 levels (p99, not the mean: the Phong wrong twin's mean was too forgiving on a mostly dark picture)
